passage: Ishita here, from flat 4A. When Aditi moved into 4B, I barely noticed. Then she kept "happening" to be at the lift at eight. First there was only a nod. Next she asked where the laundry was. A few days later she carried my parcel up from the gate and set it at my door, hovering a second too long before a small smile. She looked nervous each time, but she kept coming back. On Friday she asked if I wanted to share an auto to the market, and I said yes. Honestly, I would never have knocked on her door myself; I'd have waited for the awkwardness to pass. I can't be sure what she felt, maybe she was only being polite, but now we have a market plan for Sunday.

qa.q: What did Aditi carry up for Ishita?
qa.a: Aditi carried Ishita's parcel up from the gate.

qa.q: What might Aditi have been feeling as she hovered at Ishita's door?
qa.a: Aditi was probably nervous and hopeful, since Ishita noticed the hovering and the small smile, though Ishita admits she cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Aditi try next after the shared auto ride?
qa.a: Aditi could keep the small, repeated contact going, such as a chat at the lift or an invitation for tea, so the friendship keeps growing.

qa.q: Why might Ishita not have started the friendship herself?
qa.a: Ishita says she would never have knocked, so she may also fear awkwardness, and Aditi's small steps made it easy to say yes.

grounding: Aditi reaches out to a neighbour through small repeated contact instead of waiting to be invited.

passage: Friday night. Diary, Rashmi reporting: I finally said more than 'hi' to the man across the corridor. For six weeks I've heard Ramesh's pressure cooker whistle at 8 every evening and wondered if he's as alone in this building as I am. I kept waiting for him to knock. He didn't. Tonight I had extra lemon pickle from home, so I knocked instead, heart going like a drum. He looked surprised, then pleased. We talked for four minutes about the water timings and the lift that's always broken. That's all. But on Monday I'll ask if he knows a good vegetable vendor, and maybe on Wednesday I'll say hi at the gate without rehearsing it first. Small and repeated, that's the plan. Awkward is fine. Awkward is better than another silent week.

qa.q: At what time does Ramesh's pressure cooker whistle?
qa.a: Ramesh's pressure cooker whistles at 8 every evening.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling while knocking on the door?
qa.a: Rashmi felt nervous, heart going like a drum, but hopeful enough to knock.

qa.q: What is Rashmi's plan, and why is it a good one?
qa.a: Small repeated contacts, like asking about a vegetable vendor on Monday and saying hi at the gate, because friendship grows through many short meetings.

qa.q: How might Ramesh have felt when Rashmi knocked?
qa.a: Ramesh looked surprised, then pleased, perhaps glad that someone in the building reached out first.

grounding: A diary shows the fear of awkwardness with a neighbour and the choice to stop waiting and build contact through small repeated steps.

Gurleen: bring three, my friend Bhoomi might join
Varun: done. three chai
(the next week)

Gurleen: obviously 😄
